recovery_analysis.thesis: FORENSIC DISTRESSED FOCUS: 100% state-owned rail monopoly operating 82% of Ukraine's freight. $595M 2026 and $300M 2028 notes price in deep 36% haircut; base restructuring expectation is standalone 3-year maturity extension + partial PIK yielding $71.50 recovery.

annotations.note: Halted payments Jan-26 on $703m Jul-26 & $351.9m 2028 LPNs; FY25 rev $2.19bn, Q126 loss $178m; pursuing restructuring + 30% freight tariff hike.

annotations.source: J.P. Morgan / Morgan Stanley Distressed Credit
annotations.note: The $595M 8.25% notes due July 2026 and $300M 7.875% notes due July 2028 were extended by 24 months in August 2022. Following Ukraine's $20.5B sovereign Eurobond restructuring in August 2024 (37% nominal haircut), market consensus expects UZ to execute standalone commercial maturity extensions (3-5 years) with partial PIK coupon features rather than deep principal haircuts due to its essential defense and grain export mandate.

annotations.source: EBRD / EIB / World Bank RELINC Filings
annotations.note: Over $1.4B in non-repayable grants and subsidized loans committed by the EU Solidarity Lanes, EIB, and EBRD. Capital expenditures are heavily focused on converting strategic cross-border lines from 1520mm Russian broad-gauge to 1435mm European standard-gauge (Chop-Uzhhorod and Lviv-Warsaw corridors), permanently integrating Ukrainian rail into the EU single market.

annotations.source: Cabinet of Ministers / UZ Investor Disclosures
annotations.note: Freight volumes rebounded to 175M tonnes in 2024A driven by naval de-mining of the Greater Odesa Black Sea corridor and European steel mill demand for Metinvest iron ore. State-approved freight tariff indexation (+70% in July 2022 plus ongoing inflation adjustments) and passenger social subsidies maintain positive EBITDA (~$380M).

annotations.topic: Forensic Recovery: Liquidation Scrap Floor vs Restructured Value
annotations.note: Physical asset base includes >80,000 wagons, 1,150 active locomotives, and 16,800+ km of operated track. Scrap steel and unencumbered rolling stock liquidation floor is $38.00. Base-case going-concern restructuring value is $68.00 - $74.00, offering attractive asymmetric risk/reward for high-beta credit portfolios.
Entered RD/D after Jan-26 coupon suspension & Jul-26 $703m missed bullet (~$1.1bn debt). Bondholders rejected 20% haircut; 30% freight tariff hike effective Aug 1, 2026.

verdict.stance: Distressed Hold / Selective Default (RD) & Active Restructuring on $1.1bn Debt
verdict.summary: Ukrzaliznytsia entered technical default in Jan-26 by halting payments on its $703m Jul-26 and $351.9m 2028 LPNs after FY25 core EBITDA ex-grants turned negative (-UAH 141m) and Q126 posted a $178m (UAH 7.9bn) loss. Restructuring talks and a 30% freight tariff hike are underway.

positives: 30% freight tariff hike effective Aug 1, 2026 meaningfully improves operating cash flow baseline.
Essential wartime sovereign logistics backbone backed by €130m EBRD emergency liquidity reallocation.
Bondholder ad-hoc committee pushback forced tariff reform rather than purely punitive haircuts.
negatives: Active selective default (RD/D): suspended Jan-26 coupons and missed >$703m July-26 bullet maturity.
~$1.1bn Eurobond stack in contested restructuring after initial 20% haircut / 2033 proposal was rejected.
Severe Russian strikes on rail/power infrastructure and chronic loss-making passenger segment.
